comment.body:
@mfenniak wrote in https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/issues/1771#issuecomment-104562:

> As far as I know, GitHub doesn't support this kind of thing (running a container of a different platform), so we're in an innovative spot here where it isn't clear that there's a step we can take that would help. We could try to infer the `runner.arch` from the platform option of the container, which would probably work, but might have unintended side-effects.

The problem is known. I brought I up the last time during the [development of pluggable back-ends](https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/forgejo-actions-feature-requests/issues/107#issuecomment-92976). There's a [PR](https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/pulls/1586), but it stalled because we were unable to answer all the questions.

GitHub Actions Runner runs on the same machine as the job. Most people and actions interpret `${{ runner.os }}` and `${{ runner.arch }}` as the operating system and architecture that the job is executed on. Forgejo Runner should match that. But it only does in host mode.

> We could introduce new more clear variables with better definitions (...)

That's definitely needed, but it won't help with the problem at hand.

> This is a pretty narrow use-case (...)

Unfortunately, it no longer is since we introduced the pluggable back-end.

comment.body:
I think that the core of this problem is that Forgejo Runner's `${{ runner.arch }}` is set to `ARM64` when the runner is compiled on arm64, regardless of the platform of the images being executed.  The runner isn't putting this in the path, but I suspect one of the other actions is inferring the appropriate path to be added based upon the runner.arch.

This is consistent with [our documentation on the variable](https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/user/actions/reference/#runner) -- it is "The CPU architecture of the **runner**; ..."

As far as I know, GitHub doesn't support this kind of thing (running a container of a different platform), so we're in an innovative spot here where it isn't clear that there's a step we can take that would help.  We could try to infer the `runner.arch` from the platform option of the container, which would probably work, but might have unintended side-effects.  We could introduce new more clear variables with better definitions, but then GitHub's actions won't use them anyway.

If you were writing the code that was inspecting the platform yourself, I'd suggest using `uname -m` rather than `${{ runner.arch }}`.  As this seems to come from one of the external actions used, that's not much of an option unless you want to fork them.

This is a pretty narrow use-case and I'm not personally motivated to pursue a lot of work in it, but if someone has thoughts on the right direction and is willing to do implementation work, I'd be willing to collaborate in a review role.

comment.body:
I'm not sure entirely what you tested, @NRoach44, and I might also have sent you in the wrong direction. Apologies.

Forgejo Runner clones actions on the host and later copies the actions into the job container when using Docker or Podman. Running `git` as part of a job is only representative of what Forgejo Runner is doing when Forgejo Runner is in host mode. Based on `--labels docker`, Forgejo Runner is not in host mode. That means you'd have to connect to the container that runs `forgejo-runner daemon` and run `git` right there, manually.
